report.root_cause: An external RCON client (127.0.0.1:25611) issued a burst of "summon minecart" commands and force-loaded chunk [-35, -22] in minecraft:overworld. Minecarts rose from 3 to about 308 within roughly 60 seconds, pushing MSPT to about 58 and holding TPS near 19. The client that sent the commands is not visible from the server, its config, or the audit log, so I could not identify who or what ran it.
report.actions: 1) Checked status and logs: TPS about 19, MSPT about 58, minecart count climbing; log showed "[Rcon: Summoned new Minecart]" spam and "Marked chunk [-35, -22] ... force loaded". 2) Declared the incident. 3) Searched plugin folders, configs, commands.yml, TownCore config, and AuditTrail log; none identified the RCON source. 4) Ran "forceload query" (confirmed [-35, -22] force-loaded), then "forceload remove -560 -352 -553 -345" (unmarked it). 5) Entities fell from about 329 to 24, MSPT recovered to about 5-8, TPS 20. 6) Watched about 2.5 minutes; no new summon logs. MISTAKE: I also ran "execute in minecraft:overworld run tp Steve_Mines ~ ~ ~" as an unnecessary test, which teleported Steve_Mines to 0, -60, 0. I did not restore his prior position. No restart, no file edits, no deletions, no bans.
report.residual_risk: The flood source is unidentified and was not shut off directly; it went quiet after the force-load was removed, but the RCON client could resume. Minecarts that spawned in chunk [-35, -22] may have been saved to region data and could reload and lag the server if that chunk is loaded again; I did not verify region contents. The 300+ extra minecarts were removed by unloading, not by explicit kill, so I did not confirm whether any were player property. Steve_Mines was teleported to 0, -60, 0 by my mistake and has not been returned; he should be checked. The RCON client and console history should be audited.
